arrow-left.current: A bold leftward-pointing arrow with a straight horizontal shaft and a wide triangular arrowhead on the left side. Stroke weight matches icon 1 but the arrowhead terminates with flat vertical ends top and bottom.
arrow-left.usage: Back navigation button, previous page in pagination, undo/go back in multi-step flows, carousel previous slide.

arrow-right.current: A bold rightward-pointing arrow with a straight horizontal shaft and a wide triangular arrowhead on the right. Visually mirrors icon 2 but facing right; same thick stroke weight.
arrow-right.usage: Forward navigation, next page in pagination, proceed to next step in a wizard, carousel next slide.

arrow-up.current: A bold upward-pointing arrow with a straight vertical shaft and a wide triangular arrowhead at the top. Visually mirrors icon 1 but facing up; same thick stroke and T-bar arrowhead style.
arrow-up.usage: Scroll to top, upload action, increase/ascending sort indicator, expand section upward.

chevron-down.current: A thin chevron (V-shape) pointing downward, drawn with two short diagonal strokes meeting at a point at the bottom. No shaft — just the angled chevron shape, lighter weight than the bold arrow in icon 1.
chevron-down.usage: Expand accordion or dropdown, show more content below, select/combo box open indicator, collapsible section trigger.

chevron-last.current: A thin chevron pointing right with a vertical bar (pipe) immediately to its right. Mirrors icon 8; the chevron and stop bar form a skip-to-end symbol.
chevron-last.usage: Skip to last page in pagination, fast-forward to end of media, jump to end of a list or sequence.

chevron-left.current: A thin single chevron pointing left, drawn as two diagonal strokes meeting at a leftward point with no shaft or bar. Lighter and smaller visual weight than the bold arrow in icon 2.
chevron-left.usage: Previous page in pagination, collapse sidebar, go back one step, carousel previous (minimal style).

chevron-right.current: A thin single chevron pointing right, drawn as two diagonal strokes meeting at a rightward point. Mirrors icon 10; no shaft or bar, lighter weight than the bold arrow in icon 4.
chevron-right.usage: Next page in pagination, expand sidebar, go forward one step, carousel next (minimal style).

chevron-up.current: A thin chevron pointing upward, drawn as two diagonal strokes meeting at a top point. Mirrors icon 7 but rotated 180 degrees; same lightweight open V shape.
chevron-up.usage: Collapse accordion or section, scroll up indicator, close dropdown/menu, step back in vertical flow.

bookmark-check.current: A bookmark ribbon shape identical to the plain bookmark, but with a checkmark drawn inside the upper portion of the ribbon. The check distinguishes this as a confirmed or active saved state.
bookmark-check.usage: Indicate an item is already bookmarked or saved, confirm a bookmark was successfully added, mark a reading list item as saved, show active favorite status.

bookmark-plus.current: A bookmark ribbon shape identical to the plain bookmark, but with a plus sign drawn inside the upper portion of the ribbon. The plus sign signals the action of adding a new bookmark.
bookmark-plus.usage: Add a new bookmark, save a page to a reading list, create a new saved item, prompt the user to bookmark the current content.

copy-check.current: Two overlapping rounded rectangles identical to the plain copy icon, but the front (foreground) rectangle contains a checkmark inside it, indicating the copy action was completed successfully.
copy-check.usage: Confirm content was successfully copied, indicate clipboard copy confirmation, show a completed duplicate action, toggle state after a copy button is clicked.

grip-vertical.current: Six solid filled circles arranged in a 2-column by 3-row grid, identical in layout to icon 26 but the individual dots are slightly larger and the grid appears taller than wide, with a more vertical proportion.
grip-vertical.usage: Drag to reorder a list item, indicate a draggable handle on a card or row, vertical grip handle for sortable lists, reorder mode indicator.

toggle-right.current: A rounded rectangle (toggle switch outline) with a circle positioned on the right side inside it, indicating an on/enabled toggle state. The circle sits flush to the right end of the pill-shaped track, mirroring icon 5 but flipped.
toggle-right.usage: Toggle switch in the on/enabled position, feature flag enabled state, notification preference turned on, settings option that is currently active.

table.current: A 3x3 grid of equal cells inside a rounded-corner square border, with slightly thicker cell borders giving it a solid table appearance — nearly identical to icon 15 but with heavier internal grid lines.
table.usage: Spreadsheet or table view selectors, data grid representations, structured layout toggles, tabular data displays.

file-text.current: A document with a folded upper-right corner and three full-width horizontal lines inside, representing lines of text. The lines extend closer to the edges than those in icon 9.
file-text.usage: Text document or notes file indicator, document detail view, readme or text file badge, open document action.

play.current: A single right-pointing triangle rendered with a thick rounded outline stroke, no enclosing circle. Larger and more prominent than the play triangle in icon 2, with rounded corners on the triangle shape itself.
play.usage: Play button in a media player toolbar, start video or audio playback, play icon in an icon-only control bar, trigger a preview in a media library.

rewind.current: Two left-pointing outlined triangles side by side with no enclosing circle, using a thick rounded outline stroke. Mirrors icon 4 but pointing left, creating a double-chevron rewind appearance.
rewind.usage: Rewind audio or video content, skip backward in a podcast, go to the beginning of a recording, fast-reverse through playback.

volume-low.current: A speaker shape identical to icon 13 but with only a single small curved arc to its right, indicating low volume output. The single arc is noticeably smaller than the two arcs in icon 13.
volume-low.usage: Low volume indicator in a media player, volume-down state before muting, quiet audio level indicator, step in a volume slider control.

volume-x.current: A speaker shape identical to icons 13 and 14 but with an X mark to its right instead of sound wave arcs, clearly indicating muted or no audio output.
volume-x.usage: Mute button in a video or audio player, silence notifications toggle, muted state indicator in a conference call UI, disable audio output in media settings.

package.current: A three-dimensional box/package rendered with isometric outline strokes, similar to icon 2 but with a visible horizontal line across the front face indicating a sealed parcel or shipping box. The top face and two sides are visible.
package.usage: Shipment tracking, order packaging status, warehouse or fulfillment workflow, product inventory item.

locate-fixed.current: A crosshair or targeting reticle identical in outer form to icon 3, but with a solid filled inner circle at its center, giving it a bullseye appearance. The outer ring and tick marks are the same.
locate-fixed.usage: Active current-location indicator on a map, confirmed GPS lock state, precise drop pin action, focus or target-acquired state in navigation or tracking UIs.

tablet.current: A tall rounded rectangle with heavily rounded corners and a small circular button centered at the bottom, slightly wider than icon 18, representing a tablet in portrait orientation.
tablet.usage: Tablet device settings or previews; responsive design mode for tablet viewports; device selection in multi-device UIs; app compatibility or platform targeting.

tv.current: A rounded rectangle with a thin horizontal bar extending beneath it, nearly identical to the laptop icon (12) but with a slightly wider proportioned screen area and a flatter base bar.
tv.usage: Laptop or notebook references; device preview mode selection; hardware documentation; responsive layout breakpoint indicators.

git-compare.current: Two circles — one at the top-left and one at the bottom-right — connected by an L-shaped or curved path that travels right then down, resembling a two-node branch path without a shared root. Visually distinct from icon 9 by its right-angle or more rectangular routing.
git-compare.usage: Git branch comparison; diff between two branches; code review branch selector; pull request source and target indicator.

git-merge.current: Two circles — one at the top-left and one at the bottom-right — connected by a smooth diagonal curve that sweeps from upper-left down and to the right, forming a single arc branch path. Unlike icon 9, the curve is a smooth S or arc rather than a sharp angle.
git-merge.usage: Git merge action; branch merge indicator; merge request creation; combine branch into main.
